content.thinking:
I need to design a rising kraken in an Overwatch-style look: a humanoid mantle with crest and tentacle beard, eight large curling tentacles with suckers, glowing cyan rune accents, clean bold panel shapes, and roughly a 6-meter scale.

For the skeleton, I'm planning a pelvis root with a spine chain rising through chest, neck, and head, then branching into six floor-planted tentacle legs and two raised, curling arm-tentacles, plus four shorter beard tendrils from the head -- working out joint names, parenting, and path points for each chain.

Now I'm figuring out the body shape: sweeping the spine chain with varying radii for a broad chest tapering toward the neck, then shaping the head with a scaled skull sphere and a fin-like crest extruded along the back.

Still defining the crest outline...

Now I'm placing glowing cyan eyes relative to the head position, facing forward, with brow ridges as rotated boxes. For the jaw I'm setting up tendril chains sprouting downward-forward using a catmull-rom chain generator with parent joints.

Writing sucker rings...

I'm thinking about the suckers' orientation—since tentacles arch up then curl down to the floor, I want the underside facing inward/down to stay visible, so angling them around 150 degrees works better than true underside placement. Now I'm planning the tentacle paths themselves, starting at radius 0.6 from the body at y=2.0 and arching outward before descending.

Each of the eight tentacles sweeps outward along its azimuth direction, rising to a peak around y=2.5, then descending through several points toward floor contact near radius 4.1, with the tip curling back upward afterward to form a natural hook shape.

I'll allow slight floating of about 0.01 and set the floor at y=0.13 so the lowest tentacle points rest near it. I'm considering whether to add a water base or ripple disc beneath the kraken for a diorama feel, but it would spread the bounding box too much given the tentacles already reach out to 4.6, so I'll likely keep it minimal rather than adding a large water element.

Instead I'll add a small dark teal disc, about 0.08 in height, that touches the floor directly to guarantee ground contact, letting the tentacle tips sink slightly into it for a natural resting pose. For the tentacle rigging I'm planning 8-point catmull chains with 8 joints each across 8 tentacles, plus spine, head, and beard segments, tallying up the total joint count for the rig.

Each tentacle chain will parent from the pelvis root, with the tentacle bases nestled inside a large scaled hemispherical mantle sphere centered near the pelvis to give the body mass that the limbs visibly emerge from.

I'll plan eight tentacles total: five sprawled low along the ground and two side ones arching upward and curling inward, defined by a shared parametric function using azimuth angle, reach distance, peak height, and curl style so each limb's path can vary while sharing the same generation logic.

For sucker placement I'll scale the sucker radius relative to the tentacle's local radius at each point along the sweep, placing around 14 suckers between t=0.12 and 0.92 with alternating inward-facing angles. I'll also add small dorsal spikes running along the top of the tentacle at intervals.

For coloring, I'm picking a warm tan/coral accent for the spikes and suckers, with a cyan glow for secondary highlights. Since glowing effects can't just be painted on, I'm planning to add a separate thin swept tube running along the tentacle's length colored cyan to simulate a glowing rune stripe.

I realize a plain swept path would rigidly follow just the starting bone and tear during flex, so instead I'll bind the sweep to the whole bone chain so it skins properly. I'll taper the glow radius along the length and place two such glowing lines per tentacle at offset angles so they read clearly against the dark skin.

For shading, I'm leaning toward a toon-style cel approach rather than flat paint—using a cel function that derives shadow tones from the surface normal for bold color blocking. I'm settling on a deep indigo back and teal belly, dividing the body into sectors rather than relying purely on paint so each region gets distinct coloring.

Still adding texture and resolution details...

I'm deciding to add armored plates to the chest and shoulders for a more polished, sci-fi kraken look, with bevelled coral-grey plates and cyan glow trim, extruded from a chest outline.

To figure out exact placement, I'm working out the chest surface geometry—finding the proper facing direction and radius so the plate sits correctly against the body's curve, using a ray cast against the body surface to get accurate positioning.

Now I'm sketching the body proportions: pelvis at [0,1.9,0] rising through spine points up to the neck at [0,3.8,.25], with a radius profile that bulges around the belly then tapers down to .42 at the neck, ending with a rounded cap at the chain's tip.

I'm placing the head at [0,3.95,.35] with roughly .55 radius, pushing the crest up to about 5.2 and the full raised-tentacle height near 5.4. Then I'm adding two armored shoulder spheres near [±.85,3.3,.1] off the chest joint, and rooting the raised tentacle-arm chains at the shoulders instead of the pelvis so they read as arms, each with six joints branching off the chest.

Now I'm mapping out the curling path for those arm chains, giving them a slimmer .3 radius tapering from .28 at the root, with the arm curving outward then hooking back inward toward the head. For the remaining ground tentacles I'm spacing eight of them around the pelvis by azimuth angle, aiming for a total of two upper arm-tentacles plus eight lower ones spread around the body.

Defining the ground limb profile points...

Checking the next point, the radius stays within floor tolerance so it's fine. I'm also building the water disc base as a lathe shape with a subtle rim profile, colored a teal-blue, plus flat foam ripple rings at each tentacle's ground contact point.

Still writing scene setup...

Still shaping head details...

Confirming the thickness axis is perpendicular to the slanted eye direction, then placing glowing cyan sphere eyes near the front of the skull, positioning them just below where the ellipsoid's front radius extends.

Working out the brow rotation direction for angry vs sad expressions, concluding inner ends should slant lower with rotation scaled by side sign times 20 degrees. Now positioning the jaw joint and beard tendril anchor points in head-local coordinates.

For the jaw mesh and beard tendrils, I'm mapping out four chains rooted near the mouth that curl down and forward toward the chest, tapering in radius from thick at the base to thin at the tip.

I'll add a jaw sphere with upward tusk spikes at the corners, plus a face plate ridge on the skull. Then I'm adding spiky shoulder pauldrons positioned on the chest bone, colored in a dark slate armor tone with cyan trim.

Now I'm detailing the chest plate with a glowing cyan diamond rune on the front, and planning a dorsal fin of coral spikes running along the spine using the body sweep's tangent direction so they project outward from the back.

I'm also adding glowing paint lines across the body at angled offsets to suggest front-facing chest runes, confirming that the line path can be swept along the spine bone, and settling on a coral tone for the sucker details.

I'm sketching out a tentacle builder function that takes a name, parent, control points, and base radius, then constructs a chain by resampling a catmull-rom curve into joints for the tentacle's bone structure.

Now I'm defining how the sweep tapers along the tentacle, shrinking the radius toward a small rounded tip, then placing suckers at intervals along the surface using the sweep's position and angle lookup, aiming for around 13 suckers per tentacle to keep part counts manageable across the full creature.

Next I'm adding dorsal spikes riding the bone frame at points along the length, each anchored to the surface hit point with a short tapered cone shape, and glowing cyan rune lines following a separate thin sweep along the tentacle for a decorative energy effect.

I'll skip the glow dots and ring loops since they add too much complexity, keeping just the dual tube lines at ±35 plus suckers and spikes. Now I'm finalizing the metadata export with name, description, style, and commit, and sorting out which imports are actually needed versus unused.

Writing paint variables...

Settling on a coral-gold accent palette with deep armor plates and light trim, then moving into writing the actual build script with imports for the builder, path, paint, and glow utilities.

Defining the kraken's skeleton...

Still defining body profile...

Now I'm adding a glowing forehead rune, placing a small diamond-shaped decal on the skull surface by calculating the correct z-position based on the head's curvature, with a slight tilt to match the surface angle.

Next I work out crest placement on top of the skull, checking that its front and back edges stay within the skull's silhouette at that height; the initial height comes out too tall, so I scale the crest outline down by a factor to keep the total figure height reasonable.

Now I move on to finishing the eyes, then adding a beard, shoulder armor plates, arms, ground tentacles, and water effects before returning the completed body. I set up a ripple torus for water foam near the base, attach a pelvis bone, and add a cluster of bone spikes across the shoulders at varied angles for a spiky, armored look.

For the chest plate, I compute a surface wrapper around the body sweep so I can sample nearest points at different heights to extrude plate shapes that hug the torso's contour, keeping the shoulder spheres excluded from that surface so the plates only follow the body form.

To fix the floating gap, I'll shrink the plate to 0.75 scale and reposition it closer to the body surface with reduced thickness, which cuts the edge float down to a small visible gap that still reads as armor flaring. Then I'm layering an inner glow diamond slightly in front of the plate's surface, and starting on the gold rune bands for the belt/ring.

Now I'm writing the arm tentacle generator, defining root/shoulder joints at the chest, a reusable tentacle function parameterized by root radius, sucker angle, and sucker count, with left/right mirroring and proper joint naming, importing the Joint type for the parent parameter...

Still writing tentacle code...

Writing tentacle generation logic...

I'm settling on 6 ground tentacles plus the 2 arms for 8 total appendages, checking that their base points stay within the pelvis sphere for proper attachment, and now placing a foam ring torus at the floor contact point of one tentacle for visual grounding.

Next I'm building the water surface as a lathe shape rotated around the pelvis, defining its outline from the axis outward and back to form a closed, flat disc with a mottled color treatment.

Now I'm turning to the beard, setting up x-offsets and length factors for four symmetric strands, then plotting each strand's points as they curve downward and outward from the chin, adjusting depth and spread based on the strand's length multiplier.

Each strand becomes a tapering tentacle-like chain curling forward at the tip, with a skin-tone base color and a slightly deeper tip shade for contrast. Finally I'm adding a dark interior ellipsoid at the jaw to suggest the mouth cavity.

Now I'm placing the lower jaw shape and small bone-colored tusks jutting upward from it, then tucking a dark inner sphere beneath the snout to fake mouth depth before writing the file and double-checking all the color/scale constants are defined consistently.

Next I'm shaping the coral frill extrusion along the skull's sides, positioning its outline with sharp unbeveled corners near the back, then sizing the frill's ear-like flare to fit proportionally before moving on to designing the crest coloring.

Writing extrude outline...
